column1: 24:5|What can reasonably be inferred about the ban on Hannah openly taking notes during a visit?|It helps her preserve the appearance of an ordinary diner while gathering information.|It makes written reports unnecessary after she leaves a restaurant.|It ensures that staff members know which interactions will be evaluated.|It prevents her from accepting assignments at unfamiliar restaurants.|She must collect detailed information without openly recording it; posing as a normal customer is what makes the assignment covert.

14:2|Which conclusion about the observed brain response is best supported?|The change depended on whether participants viewed social or nonsocial images, rather than being a uniform increase in activity.|The treatment increased reward-circuit activity equally for faces and cars.|A change in brain activity established lasting improvements in everyday social behavior.|The placebo group and oxytocin group could not be compared because neither received a nasal spray.|The response increased for faces but decreased for cars. This supports a stimulus-dependent effect, while the paragraph does not report long-term behavioral outcomes.

3:2|Which inference best explains why schooling support might need to address family finances as well as classroom access?|Some families depend on income from children whose continued work conflicts with attending school.|Providing skills training has eliminated every reason children leave school.|Parents who depend on a child's earnings necessarily oppose education for all their children.|Physical access to a state school is the only obstacle mentioned.|The brothers' earnings are described as necessary for family survival, while the program also tries to raise family income. Together these facts indicate a financial obstacle beyond enrolling a child.

23:6|What does the mayor's position imply about efforts to keep the island attractive to families?|Improvements in education could be offset by a higher financial burden on residents.|The tax increase must already have caused every young family to leave.|A delay in imposing the tax guarantees that the island will be exempt permanently.|Bringing children to parliament would itself change the legal tax rate.|The mayor improves education to retain families but warns that higher taxes would drive young people away. The two policies can therefore work in opposing directions.

11:1|Which inference about the FAO initiative is most strongly supported?|It promotes wider use of a practice that already has a substantial existing base of participants.|It introduces insect consumption to regions where no one has previously tried it.|It is intended solely to provide material for a television documentary.|The list of edible species establishes that all insect species are safe to eat.|An estimated two billion people already eat insects, yet the FAO is promoting their farming and consumption. The initiative expands an existing practice rather than inventing one.

24:0|Which implication for physical retailers follows from the account?|They may need to offer distinctive in-person service as more spending moves online.|The growth of online spending shows that customers no longer enter physical shops.|Mystery-shopping results establish that every store already exceeds customer expectations.|Recruiting more mystery shoppers guarantees an increase in retail sales.|The account links online spending with a need to measure experiences customers cannot get online. Evaluation could help stores compete through a distinctive in-person experience, without guaranteeing sales.

28:0|How would an evaluation of Kelley's proposal most reasonably reflect his stated rationale?|It would examine health outcomes as well as academic or cognitive outcomes.|It would treat exam results as the only potentially relevant outcome.|It would assume that later starts remove all causes of sleep deprivation.|It would determine effectiveness solely from the age of the school administrators.|The proposal is justified by both cognitive and exam benefits and health effects. Assessing only one category would omit part of its rationale.

0:1|What can be inferred about the role of the genealogical researcher?|Connecting a named sender with a living descendant required work beyond simply recovering the bottle.|He personally saw the grandfather place the message in the bottle.|The bottle itself contained Angela's current Berlin address.|He established that the card was written specifically for the granddaughter.|The letter reached a museum, and a genealogical researcher then tracked Angela down. That sequence indicates a separate identification process, not an address or intended recipient stated on the card.

14:5|Which finding would address the specific limitation Frith identifies?|Evidence that the observed neural response is accompanied by a useful change in participants' behavior.|A repeat scan showing the same brain effect without any behavioral observations.|A larger number of photographs of faces than photographs of cars.|An account of how quickly the research team prepared the nasal spray.|Frith distinguishes an effect on brain activity from the practical behavioral benefit needed for treatment value. Behavioral evidence directly addresses that gap.

9:5|What can be inferred from the offers to sell meteorite fragments shortly after the incident?|Some people treated the event as an immediate commercial opportunity, regardless of the unsettled speculation about its cause.|The sale listings proved the claim about a weapons test.|The government meeting established the authenticity of every offered fragment.|All witnesses agreed on what had caused the event before any listings appeared.|Sales offers appeared within hours amid confusion and competing claims. Their appearance shows an attempt to profit, not verification of either the fragments or a proposed cause.

28:4|What concern about the traditional work schedule is implied by the discussion?|A schedule convenient for those who set it may not be equally well suited to younger workers.|Older supervisors are necessarily less productive than teenage employees.|The same starting hour is proposed as ideal for every age group.|Staggered hours would eliminate the need for coordination among employees.|The passage says older bosses maintain hours best for them and then suggests different starts for different ages. This implies that the preferences of decision makers need not match every worker's rhythms.

15:3|What does Carle's difficulty finding an acceptable car imply about his rules?|A French brand name alone did not establish that a product met his purchase criteria.|Every product sold by a French company was automatically allowed.|Imported cars became acceptable whenever their price was low enough.|The origin of a product mattered only for food and drink.|The affordable French-brand car models were made overseas and therefore were not acceptable. Manufacturing origin mattered beyond the nationality associated with the brand.

29:4|Which principle is implied by Singh's emphasis on contingency planning?|A useful safety plan must address reasonable behavior after a failure, not merely assume failures never occur.|A mature aviation industry can dispense with procedures for component failures.|Any failed component necessarily causes a catastrophic crash.|Reliability requirements can be established from payload capacity alone.|Even an established industry returns aircraft to the gate for small component failures. Singh's proposed response focuses on what a vehicle does when a failure occurs.

7:5|What can be inferred about the stage at which a newly proposed element symbol becomes final?|Receiving a proposal does not itself complete the process, because objections can still be raised during review.|Any proposal becomes permanent as soon as researchers submit two letters.|Only the researchers proposing a symbol can comment on its suitability.|A five-month review is mentioned as a method for producing more atoms.|The submission is followed by public review, and the example describes a symbol changed after objections. Submission and final acceptance are therefore distinct stages.

20:1|Which broader effect of the ice-cream shop is supported by Ingabire's account?|Employment there can expand economic options for workers and their families as well as sell a product.|The business has already persuaded every Rwandan consumer to buy ice cream.|The shop provides wages only when employees donate all earnings to relatives.|Curiosity about a new dessert is sufficient by itself to guarantee permanent profits.|Ingabire contrasts unemployment with earning money, helping family, and having a future vision. Those changes extend beyond the dessert itself; universal demand or guaranteed profit is not established.

18:0|Why would a conservation researcher reasonably value evidence such as the droppings described?|Indirect traces can provide useful information about animals that are rarely observed directly.|Such traces make it possible to count the entire national wolf population in one visit.|Finding one trace proves that wolves no longer face any threats.|Indirect traces establish that the researcher has seen the animal producing them.|Wolf sightings are rare, yet the tracker is excited by droppings. This indicates that indirect signs have informational value without guaranteeing an exact count or a sighting.

26:2|Which interpretation best captures a distinction in Traeger-Muney's position?|She can recognize concerns about inequality while objecting to treating wealthy people uniformly as a negative group.|Her criticism of media coverage requires denying that inequality is a legitimate subject of debate.|She considers every statement made by the Occupy movement equally objectionable.|She argues that wealthy people should never face criticism of any kind.|She calls the movement good and acknowledges its important points, but criticizes its generalized portrayal of the one percent. Agreement on an issue and objection to blanket characterization can coexist.

7:5|What lesson about proposed scientific symbols is illustrated by the Cp example?|Community review can reveal a conflict with an existing meaning that a proposed symbol needs to avoid.|Changing a symbol requires changing the atomic structure of the element.|A symbol is rejected whenever any two researchers disagree about an element's properties.|The final symbol must preserve the first letter of every earlier proposal.|Cp was replaced because it referred to another substance. The example shows why checking established usage can matter when choosing a new symbol.

8:3|Which requirement for expanding the described driverless-car technology is implied?|Expanding operation to many more roads would require dealing with the limited coverage of detailed maps.|Producing more vehicles alone would remove the need for road information.|Detailed maps already cover nearly all public roads in California.|Licensing the technology establishes that real-time information limits have already been solved.|The cars require prior high-definition scans, but only about 2000 of more than 170000 road miles are mapped. Broader geographic use therefore needs a solution to that coverage limitation.

7:6|Which inference about the proposed classifications of the new elements is most reasonable?|The classifications remain tentative partly because so little material has been produced for investigation.|The predicted classifications establish that practical uses are already known.|Observing a characteristic radioactive decay provides complete knowledge of an element's bulk properties.|Difficulty in synthesizing atoms shows that no evidence of their existence can be obtained.|The language is tentative and the paragraph explicitly notes the very small number of atoms. Identification through decay signatures does not supply all properties or applications.

28:0|Which assumption underlies the proposal to adjust school starting times?|The timing of school can interact with students' biological rhythms in ways that affect their functioning.|All students have exactly the same sleep habits and health risks.|Every difference in exam results is caused by starting time.|A school's schedule has no relationship to students' opportunities for sleep.|The proposal aims to align school with natural rhythms and predicts changes in cognition and health. It therefore presumes that schedule timing can matter, without claiming it is the only cause.

8:4|Which conclusion about the effects of replacing taxis with driverless vehicles follows from the passage?|Assessing the change would need to consider employment effects on drivers, beyond the vehicles' technical operation.|The estimated taxi workforce proves that every driver would be employed by the new system.|Concern about jobs demonstrates that the vehicles cannot function technically.|All employment effects can be determined from the number of seats in a vehicle.|Conyon's concern is loss of driver employment across a large workforce. That raises a consequence distinct from whether the automated vehicle works as intended.

21:2|Which inference about Duran's changing approach to loan applications is supported?|He altered how he represented an applicant rather than merely repeating the same unsuccessful applications.|The banks approved all of his applications after he submitted his real personal details.|His eventual success establishes that his own legitimate income had necessarily risen.|The television company was described as a verified existing business with substantial revenue.|The paragraph contrasts rejected applications with real details and later applications using a false company. The evidence supports a change in representation, not an established improvement in legitimate personal creditworthiness.

25:2|Which conclusion about interpreting the city rankings is best supported?|Convenient, inexpensive transport alone is not enough information to reconstruct the study's overall rankings.|A one-euro subway fare proves that every aspect of a city's quality is superior.|All US cities were ranked below every Canadian city.|The study's discussion of crime shows that transportation cannot have any value to residents.|The rankings are linked to safety and crime, while the quoted resident also values transport. A single favorable feature does not establish the study's full criteria or exact comparisons.

10:3|What does the aquarium's response to Inky's escape imply?|Staff can learn from an unusual case without concluding that every animal requires an immediate security overhaul.|Staff concluded that other octopuses lack the ability to escape.|The escape caused the aquarium to refuse every possible replacement octopus.|Treating Inky as unusual means staff learned nothing about octopus capabilities.|The aquarium calls Inky a one-off and does not plan tighter security, yet staff are more aware of octopus capabilities. Learning and a limited response to an unusual event are compatible.

15:3|What does the exclusion of Daft Punk reveal about the rules Carle was following?|The cultural content of an item could matter even when the performers were French.|Music by a French performer was allowed regardless of the language of the lyrics.|The rules were based exclusively on whether an item could be used online.|Every English-language item was necessarily manufactured in Britain.|French performers were excluded because they sang in English. Performer nationality alone was insufficient, and lyric language was an additional consideration.

21:3|What distinction is illustrated by Duran's explanation for fleeing?|Rejecting the legitimacy of a legal authority does not itself remove exposure to its penalties.|His stated political objections prove that the charges had been withdrawn.|The bail payment eliminated every possibility of a later prison sentence.|His interpretation of his actions was shared by all the banks involved.|Duran denies the system's legitimacy but still faces a possible prison term and chooses to flee. His belief about legitimacy and the legal risk are separate matters.

2:0|Which limitation should be observed when using the described results to predict future sporting success?|An observed advantage among current pupils does not by itself establish which individuals will become elite adult athletes.|The observed pupil differences establish that birth month is the only influence on sporting success.|The study directly compared the complete adult careers of every pupil.|An advantage in average fitness guarantees that every autumn-born pupil outperforms every other pupil.|The evidence concerns measured fitness among school pupils. Predictions about individual adult careers go beyond the population and outcome described, and a group tendency is not a universal guarantee.

10:2|Which combination of evidence makes an unaided escape biologically plausible in the account?|A body capable of passing through small spaces together with examples of exploratory, problem-solving behavior.|The existence of a second octopus proves which drainpipe Inky selected.|High security establishes that no animal can leave its enclosure.|Opening a jar demonstrates that an octopus must seek companionship.|The account combines boneless bodies with documented squeezing, tool use, and tank visits. Those features support physical and behavioral plausibility, not certainty about an exact route or motive.

8:0|What can be inferred about the intended role of a passenger in the described car?|The passenger can specify a destination and request an emergency stop without using conventional steering controls.|The passenger must continuously steer while the phone supplies directions.|The stop button establishes that the vehicle has no computer-controlled operation.|The absence of pedals means passengers cannot influence any aspect of a journey.|Destination selection through the app and the stop button are explicit passenger inputs. They remain possible despite the removal of conventional driving controls.

0:0|Which inference about the bottle's eventual recipient is most strongly supported?|The message could connect generations even though its sender could not have addressed it to Angela as a person already born.|The grandfather wrote the message after meeting Angela.|The museum found the bottle exactly 101 years after Angela's birth.|The sender knew which museum would eventually exhibit the bottle.|The grandfather died six years before Angela was born, while the bottle was sent still earlier. Its later intergenerational significance did not require the sender to know Angela personally.

10:0|What is most consistent with Yarrell's interpretation of Inky's escape?|Exploration may explain the behavior without assuming that the animal was unhappy or needed another octopus.|The account proves the exact emotion Inky experienced at every stage.|Solitary behavior means that an octopus is incapable of exploring an unfamiliar place.|Leaving the tank establishes that food was unavailable there.|Yarrell rejects loneliness as a necessary account because octopuses are solitary and emphasizes curiosity. His interpretation is an explanation consistent with the observations, not direct proof of an internal emotion.

21:0|Which feature distinguishes Duran's borrowing as described from an ordinary inability to repay a loan?|The refusal to repay was intended from the outset and connected to a deliberate political purpose.|The loans became unpayable only after an unexpected loss of his own income.|The passage says the banks approved donations rather than loans.|The amount borrowed by itself determines whether a borrower had a political motive.|The paragraph says he had no intention of repayment and distributed funds to projects promoting alternatives to capitalism. That supports premeditated political intent rather than an accidental later default.
